title: Ration Planner
story:
Before life support can schedule the food printers, SIGMA needs to know how much food the trip takes.

Input: three numbers on one line: `C` crew (whole number, 1–100), `D` days (whole number, 1–365) and `R` grams per person per day (decimal, 0–5000).

Output: `Rations: X kg`, where `X` is the total food in kilograms (`C × D × R ÷ 1000`), printed with 1 decimal.

Example: `6 30 450.5` prints `Rations: 81.1 kg`.
hints: One scanf can read all three: `scanf("%d %d %lf", &crew, &days, &grams);`.
Multiply the three together, then divide by 1000 to turn grams into kilograms. Keep the result in a double.
Print with `%.1f` and spell the text exactly: `Rations: ` then the number then ` kg`.
